Code (as in drop-down): Post-hoc analysis of a trained model
Definition / decision rule: An explanation method is applied after training to the model or one of its subsystems (SHAP, LIME, Grad-CAM, probing, TCAV ...).

Code (as in drop-down): Inspection of a built-in model component
Definition / decision rule: Values of a learned component are reported and interpreted (filters, attention weights, graph weights, decision coefficients). Attention used only for pooling does not count unless its weights are analysed.
The system outputs the explanation together with the decision (rationale, caption, retrieved example, saliency network with contrastive audio).

Code (as in drop-down): Combined: built-in component and post-hoc method
Definition / decision rule: A built-in component and a post-hoc method are both reported for the decision.
Post-hoc explanations are fed back into feature construction, selection or training.
Localised: the output marks evidence on the time axis of the utterance (frame attention, Grad-CAM over time, segment or word occlusion, word-aligned evidence, time-preserving regenerated audio).
Aggregated: evidence summarised over a class, item, feature, frequency band or layer (global SHAP, descriptor ranking, filter response).
Unresolved: the output cannot be related to time from the report (e.g., weights on flattened inputs not mapped back to frames).
Named hand-crafted descriptors (MFCC, F0, energy, jitter, eGeMAPS ...).
Regions of a spectrogram or other time-frequency map, or frequency bands.
Learned filters, embeddings, hidden states or layers.
Learned weights over frames or word-aligned segments.
Principal components, boosted or otherwise transformed features.
Features shown only as indices without a mapping to named cues or words.
Human-defined concepts tested in the model (e.g., TCAV pitch) or cues and words named in a generated rationale.
Several outputs with different targets.
SHAP and its variants.
LIME, permutation importance, occlusion.
Grad-CAM(++), Integrated Gradients, DeepLIFT, LRP, gradient saliency.
Attention, learned filters, network weights, tree importance, layer probing, TCAV, decision coefficients.
Generated rationale or caption, generative or counterfactual audio, contrastive cues, cue saliency.
Plot, heat map or table.
Ranked list or prose description.
Generated text or cue phrases.
At least one audible output (replayed region, regenerated or contrastive audio).
The displayed explanation refers to acoustic evidence only (a transcript in the input alone is not enough for lexical).
The explanation also refers to words, transcript features or transcript content (incl. words quoted in a rationale).
Explanatory evidence is removed, masked, inserted or regenerated and the effect on the emotion decision is measured against a control.
Explanations compared under controlled input perturbation or across repeated runs.
Participants rate or use the explanations (incl. task performance with and without explanations).
Generated rationales are scored automatically against the input (e.g., an LLM judge checks quoted words against the transcript).
Recognition accuracy, cross-corpus accuracy, ablations, agreement between two explanation methods, or agreement with annotations alone are NOT explanation tests.
